# ScottSearch 0.1.2 — choose how much context you see

This beta adds the first requirement submitted through ScottSearch's public
request form: persistent result-detail controls for large search result sets.

## What changed

- A new **Detail** control sits beside Sort, Folder, Tag, and Modified.
- Choose **Title only** to see just each note's title, relevance score, and
  vault-relative path.
- **Default** preserves the familiar three-line preview and date/tag metadata.
- Choose **Verbose** for an unclamped excerpt centered on the earliest matching
  phrase or term.
- Set **Verbose result context** in ScottSearch settings from 20 to 1,000 source
  characters on each side; the default is 100.
- The selected detail mode persists. Switching it re-renders the ten cached
  results without repeating lexical ranking or semantic inference.
- A meaning-only match with no literal query text starts its verbose preview at
  the beginning of the note instead of pretending there was a textual match.

## Privacy and compatibility

Result presentation remains local and adds no network request. Lexical search
still needs no service. Optional semantic search sends text only to the Ollama
endpoint shown in settings. The unreleased on-device model experiment remains
excluded from this package.

One bundle supports Obsidian 1.7.2 or later on macOS, Windows, Linux, iPhone,
iPad, and Android. This is still a pre-release that needs reports from real
vault sizes, themes, and devices before a stable or Community-directory release.

## Install or update

With BRAT, use **BRAT: Check for updates to all beta plugins**, then confirm
ScottSearch reports version 0.1.2 under Community plugins.

For a manual installation, download `scottsearch-0.1.2.zip` below, unzip it,
and place the enclosed `scottsearch` folder in
`<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/`. Back up important notes before testing.

Please cycle through all three detail modes and send a sanitized
[beta report](https://github.com/c4g-john/scottsearch-for-obsidian/issues/new?template=beta_test_report.yml),
even when everything works.

## Stop or roll back

Disable or uninstall ScottSearch under **Settings → Community plugins**;
neither action deletes notes. Version 0.1.1 remains available from
[all releases](https://github.com/c4g-john/scottsearch-for-obsidian/releases)
if a result-detail problem blocks testing.
